WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
The LORD "saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid." Isaiah 44:28
"Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him"; "I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me." Isaiah 45:1 Isaiah 45:4
"He shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts." Isaiah 45:13
"The LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia", that the word spoken by Jeremiah might be fulfilled. 2 Chronicles 36:22 Ezra 1:1
His proclamation: "The LORD God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah." Ezra 1:2
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He returned the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had put in the house of his gods. Ezra 1:7
Ezra's record says the house was to be built at "the place where they offered sacrifices", its expenses "given out of the king’s house". Ezra 6:3–4
He charged the people to build the house at Jerusalem and granted materials from Lebanon. Ezra 1:2–3 Ezra 3:7
Zerubbabel and Jeshua refused the help of their neighbours, saying "we ourselves together will build unto the LORD God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us". Ezra 4:3
"Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem." Ezra 1:3
Chronicles says the exiles served the king of Babylon "until the reign of the kingdom of Persia". 2 Chronicles 36:20

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Scripture gives his first and third years only.
KING OF BABYLON, OCTOBER 539 – AUGUST 530 BC (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)

Babylon fell on 13 October 539 and Cyrus entered on 29 October (the Nabonidus Chronicle); the last tablets of his ninth year date to August 530, when his death seems to have been reported. His first full year at Babylon began in spring 538.
HERODOTUS: 29 YEARS IN ALL (ABOUT 559–530 BC)

Herodotus says he reigned "thirty years wanting one"; T. G. Pinches (1915) gives the same 29 years and adds that Cyrus ruled Media for 11 of them and Babylonia for 9. Counting back from 530 gives about 559.
KEIL (1872): REIGNED ALONE AT BABYLON FROM 536 BC
Keil gives two years to Darius the Mede first and puts Cyrus's death in 529.
No: chapters 40–66 come from a prophet of the exile, writing when Cyrus was already rising
the critical scholars of the 18th and 19th centuries, as described by G. L. Robinson (1915) and the Pulpit Commentary

On this view a prophet in Babylonia about 550–538 BC wrote of Cyrus; Robinson reports that by 1915 many critics further divided these chapters among later writers. The naming of Cyrus is, the Pulpit Commentary says, one of the main grounds of the view.[21][44]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not tell how Cyrus took Babylon, how long he reigned, or how he died.
Scripture does not name Cambyses, the son who reigned after him (the Cyrus Cylinder names him).
Scripture never says Cyrus worshipped the LORD; Isaiah says "thou hast not known me" (Isa 45:4).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textScripture calls him "Cyrus king of Persia" and "Cyrus the Persian", and Isaiah names him twice. This page treats the Cyrus of Isaiah, Chronicles, Ezra and Daniel as one king. 2 Chronicles 36:22 Ezra 1:1 Daniel 6:28 Isaiah 44:28 Isaiah 45:1

Scholars' viewIsaiah's "righteous man from the east" and "ravenous bird from the east" do not name him; that they mean Cyrus is an interpretation, held for example by G. L. Robinson (1915). Isaiah 41:2 Isaiah 46:11 [21]
